issue.title: Stop $(cmd) execution in agent-authored prompt text
issue.description:
`preprocess_prompt_late` (src/sase/llm_provider/preprocessing.py:205) runs
`process_command_substitution` (sink: src/sase/file_references.py:393,
`_execute_cmd_cached`, `subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)`) on every prompt after
protecting only disabled regions and fenced blocks. Monitor follow-up prompts
already defend against this: src/sase/monitor/followup_prompt.py:337 wraps
untrusted command output in `wrap_disabled_region`. But two agent-authored prompt
paths get no such protection, so LLM-written text is executed host-side as shell,
outside every permission gate:

1. Handoff successor prompts: persisted verbatim by
   src/sase/agent/_staged_handoff_successor.py (~lines 65-88), launched without
   approval via src/sase/axe/run_agent_successor_delivery.py (~lines 383-439),
   then macro-expanded and late-preprocessed. Any unfenced `$(...)` the previous
   agent wrote executes in the host process. Agent-authored `sase run` launch
   prompts flow the same way.
2. Workflow-interpolated LLM output: `preprocess_prompt_early` Jinja-renders
   workflow context into prompt steps (preprocessing.py ~lines 100-110, via
   src/sase/macro/workflow_executor_steps_prompt_prepare.py), and context includes
   raw prior agent responses (`context[step.name] = {"_raw": response_text}` in
   src/sase/main/query_handler/_standalone_steps.py ~line 192). `$(...)` inside a
   model response then executes during the late phase.

First re-verify both traces (line numbers may have drifted). Then implement per
the epic's `agent_cmdsub` decision. For `provenance` (default): add an explicit
prompt-authorship parameter threaded from the launch entry points into
`preprocess_prompt_late`, and skip `process_command_substitution` (and any other
host-side execution steps, but NOT macro/artifact expansion) when the prompt text
is agent-authored. Agent-authored entry points to cover: staged-handoff successor
delivery, agent-initiated `sase run`/LaunchApproval launches, and any other path
where the prompt author is an agent rather than a human. Human-typed TUI/CLI
prompts keep current behavior. Independently of the decision, wrap workflow
context values that carry model output (`_raw`, `_response`) in
`wrap_disabled_region` the way monitor output already is, so Jinja interpolation
cannot smuggle `$(...)` back into an executable region. For `wrap`: instead wrap
the entire agent-authored prompt body in a disabled region at persist/launch time.

Tests: regression tests proving (a) a handoff/launch prompt containing `$(touch
/tmp/pwn)` does not execute and the literal text survives, (b) a workflow agent
step whose response contains `$(...)` does not execute it when a later prompt step
interpolates `{{ step._raw }}`, (c) human-authored prompts still perform command
substitution, (d) macros still expand in handoff prompts under the `provenance`
choice. Place tests near existing preprocessing tests (tests/ mirrors src/
layout).

issue.title: Trust-gate command-bearing project-local config
issue.description:
SASE merges project-local config (`sase/sase.yml` found by walking up from cwd to
the nearest VCS root: src/sase/config/core.py `load_merged_config`, ~lines
562-604, local layer via `get_local_config_path` /
`discover_project_root` in src/sase/content_layout.py) with the same authority as
the user's own ~/.config/sase/sase.yml. Command-bearing keys from that local layer
are executed with `shell=True` by host-side (not permission-gated) processes:

- commit hooks: src/sase/workflows/commit/command_hooks.py:176 (`Popen(cmd,
  shell=True)`), fed from `load_merged_config()["commit_hooks"]["before"/"after"]`
- rebase gate: src/sase/workflows/commit/rebase_gate_process.py:58, fed from
  `commit_hooks.after_rebase` via `load_merged_config_for_local_path`
- file hooks: src/sase/file_hooks/runner.py:188, commands from
  `file_hooks[].command` across `load_config_layers()` including the local layer
  (src/sase/config/file_hooks.py)
- workflows/macros are also loadable from the local layer (config/core.py
  `load_macros_by_source`), and macro workflow bash steps execute at expansion
  time.

Consequence: a hostile repo adopted as a project, or an agent editing its own
workspace's sase/sase.yml, injects commands that the host-owned commit finalizer
runs with no gate — defeating the "Completion Is Host-Owned" boundary (agents must
not be able to escalate a plain file write into host-side execution).

Implement per the epic's `local_config_commands` decision. For `digest_trust`
(default): execute command-bearing local-layer config (commit_hooks,
file_hooks[].command, local-layer macro/workflow definitions that contain bash or
python steps) only when the user has acknowledged that project's current
command-bearing content, pinned to a content digest; any change requires
re-acknowledgment (direnv-style allow model). Untrusted state must not block
non-command config (display names, aliases, etc.). Design the trust store
location, the acknowledgment UX (a CLI command and/or gate prompt — never
agent-answerable), and the refusal diagnostics as part of this phase's planning.
For `user_layers_only`: stop honoring command-bearing keys from the local layer
entirely and document the migration (hooks move to user config/overlays).

This deprecates user-reaching behavior, so before implementing read the memory
notes sase/memory/sase_flags.md (a `sunset` flag is mandatory: old
run-local-commands-untrusted branch stays reachable while migrating; create it
with `sase flag new`, never by hand) and the gotchas core note (update
src/sase/default_config.yml if config keys are added). Tests must cover both flag
states, trusted/untrusted/digest-changed projects, and that an untrusted local
layer still merges its non-command keys.

issue.title: Path-component validation for repo clone dirs and project log paths
issue.description:
Two confirmed containment gaps where repo-resident (hence agent/third-party
writable) strings reach filesystem path joins without the component validation
their sibling helpers already have:

1. src/sase/_linked_repo_paths.py: `linked_repo_clone_dir` (~line 28) and
   `sidecar_repo_clone_dir` (~line 58) do `Path(host_checkout).joinpath(*SUBDIR,
   name)` then `normalize_path()` (which resolves), so a `name`/`dirname` like
   `../../../../home/user/.config/x` escapes `<checkout>/sase/repos/`. The same
   file's `external_repo_clone_dir` (~line 36) and `hidden_sidecar_clone_dir`
   (~line 66) validate components ("must be a safe path component"), proving the
   invariant is intended. Origins: `sase.yml` `repos.sidecar.custom.<role>` keys
   and `repos.linked[].name` (src/sase/_linked_repo_config_entries.py only strips
   empties), and `.sase/sdd-store.json` role keys / `repo` basenames
   (`_repo_basename("x/..") == ".."`, _linked_repo_paths.py ~line 85;
   src/sase/sdd/_store_records.py accepts any non-empty role). Reached with no
   user interaction by sidecar auto-connect/auto-sync
   (src/sase/_sidecar_auto_connect.py, src/sase/_sidecar_auto_sync.py →
   src/sase/workspace_provider/_ownership_paths.py `kind_root_for_context`) and by
   clone/materialize paths (src/sase/_linked_repo_workspaces.py →
   `ensure_git_clone_at` in src/sase/workspace_provider/_utils_checkout_clone.py,
   which has no containment check). Fix: apply the `hidden_sidecar_clone_dir`
   safe-component check (non-empty, not `.`/`..`, no `/`, `\`, NUL, no leading
   `.`, no surrounding whitespace) to `name`/`dirname` in `linked_repo_clone_dir`
   and `sidecar_repo_clone_dir`; reject non-component role keys where config and
   sdd-store records are parsed (`_sidecar_bucket_entries` /
   `_sidecars_from_raw`); and add a belt-and-suspenders containment check in
   `ensure_git_clone_at` (refuse targets not under the expected `sase/repos/`
   root when invoked for linked/sidecar clones).

2. Project-name joins under ~/.sase/projects/: `validate_sase_project_name`
   (src/sase/core/paths.py ~line 175, docstring: rejecting separators/dots "is
   what enforces containment under sase_projects_dir()") is called at somesinks
   (src/sase/_plan_approval_artifacts.py,
   src/sase/agents_sync/prompt_archive/protection.py) but NOT in five log-path
   helpers that mkdir+append at `sase_projects_dir() / project_name / ...`:
   src/sase/artifact_read_log.py `artifact_read_log_path` (~line 54),
   src/sase/memory/_read_log_events.py (~line 160), src/sase/skills/use_log.py
   (~line 130), src/sase/repo_open_log.py (~line 115),
   src/sase/memory/legacy_glossary_read_log.py (~line 56). The name can originate
   from a committed `.sase/checkout.json` `project_name`
   (src/sase/workspace_provider/marker.py `from_dict` accepts any string;
   preferred by `project_memory_name` in src/sase/main/init_memory/config.py) or
   from a git-URL basename, so a hostile checkout makes audited reads mkdir and
   append outside ~/.sase/projects/. Fix: route all five through one shared
   helper that calls `validate_sase_project_name` (decide and document the
   failure behavior: raise, or fall back to a sanitized name — prefer raising to
   match the validated sinks), and additionally validate
   `CheckoutMarker.from_dict`'s `project_name`/`project_key` at parse time.

Tests: traversal attempts (`..`-bearing and absolute names) for each fixed helper
must raise/refuse and must not create directories; valid names keep working.
Check tests/ for existing coverage of these modules and extend it.

issue.title: Shell-quote workflow interpolations, validate git refs, fix agent-guard parity
issue.description:
Three bounded hardening fixes, all independently verified:

1. Workflow bash/python step injection (per the epic's `bash_autoquote`
   decision). Sinks: src/sase/macro/workflow_executor_steps_script.py (~line 135)
   and src/sase/main/query_handler/_standalone_steps.py (~line 85) run
   Jinja-rendered templates with `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`; the Jinja env
   (src/sase/macro/workflow_executor_utils.py) has no shell-quoting filter.
   Interpolated values include macro inputs from prompt text and prior step
   outputs (including model responses). The `word` input type
   (src/sase/macro/models.py ~line 168) only rejects whitespace, so
   `$(touch${IFS}/tmp/pwn)`, `;`, and quotes all pass. Shipped injectable
   examples: src/sase/macros/file.yml (`{{ name }}` inside a bash step path) and
   src/sase/macros/json.yml (`'{{ schema }}'` — a single quote breaks out). For
   `autoquote` (default): auto-apply shlex.quote to every Jinja interpolation
   inside `bash:` steps with an explicit opt-out filter (e.g. `| raw`) for
   intentional raw interpolation; apply equivalent escaping or argument-passing
   for `python:` steps (prefer passing values via argv or env rather than
   splicing into source); update the shipped macros under src/sase/macros/ and
   src/sase/default_macros/ to stay correct under quoting. For `tighten_only`:
   instead restrict `word` to a charset allowlist `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` and audit
   shipped templates. In BOTH cases tighten `word` validation.

2. Git argument injection in VCS plugins:
   src/sase/vcs_provider/plugins/_git_core_ops.py `vcs_checkout` (~line 29)
   passes `revision` positionally to `git checkout`, and
   src/sase/vcs_provider/plugins/bare_git.py `vcs_mail` (~line 33) to `git push
   -u origin <revision>`. `revision` derives from Patch NAME / branch-map values
   in agent-writable `.sase` files (src/sase/vcs_provider/plugins/
   _git_revision_ops.py), so values like `--receive-pack=...` (push; executes a
   local command for filesystem remotes) or `-B`/`--pathspec-from-file=`
   (checkout) smuggle flags. Fix: validate candidate revisions where they are
   read (reject names starting with `-` and names failing `git check-ref-format
   --branch` or an equivalent charset check), and prefer flag-safe invocation
   forms where git's syntax allows.

3. Agent-guard detection parity: tools/_sase_install_env.py `AGENT_ENV_VARS`
   (~line 22) lists only `SASE_AGENT` and `SASE_MONITOR_ID`, but the canonical
   detector `agent_marker_present` (src/sase/agent/identity.py ~lines 34-48) also
   recognizes `SASE_AGENT_NAME` and discovered agent metadata. A process carrying
   only `SASE_AGENT_NAME` bypasses the "Global Install Is Human-Only" refusal in
   `agent_guard`. Fix: add `SASE_AGENT_NAME` to `AGENT_ENV_VARS` (keep the module
   stdlib-only; do not import sase) and add/extend the parity test the module's
   comments promise so the two sets cannot silently drift again. Read the memory
   note sase/memory/tools.md before changing anything under tools/.

Tests: injection attempts through macro args and workflow context must execute
nothing (assert via marker files/mocked subprocess); hostile revision names must
be refused before any git invocation; agent_guard must refuse under each marker
env var.

issue.title: Fix patch-lock fd double close and edit-lock acquisition races
issue.description:
Two verified defects in src/sase/ace/patch/locking.py:

1. `patch_lock` (~lines 166-184): on lock timeout the `except BlockingIOError`
   branch runs `os.close(fd)` and raises `LockTimeoutError`, but the function's
   `finally` then runs `fcntl.flock(fd, LOCK_UN)` + `os.close(fd)` on the
   already-closed fd. Single-threaded this raises OSError(EBADF) from the finally,
   replacing LockTimeoutError so handlers keying on it (e.g.
   src/sase/ace/patch/duplicate_repair.py, src/sase/ace/hooks/persistence.py)
   misclassify the failure; multi-threaded (ACE runs these in worker threads) the
   fd number can be reused by another thread between the close and the finally,
   and the finally then unlocks/closes an unrelated descriptor. Fix: restructure
   so acquisition happens before the try whose finally owns cleanup (or drop the
   close from the timeout branch and make the finally the single owner); the
   timeout path must raise LockTimeoutError exactly once with no second close.

2. `acquire_edit_lock` / `is_edit_locked` (~lines 37-91): the lock file is
   created with a plain overwrite (no O_CREAT|O_EXCL), so two processes can both
   believe they own the edit lock; liveness uses `os.kill(pid, 0)`, so a recycled
   PID makes a stale lock look held and `wait_for_edit_lock_release` can poll for
   hours. Fix: create with O_CREAT|O_EXCL (retry after stale-lock cleanup),
   record PID plus process start time (or an equivalent boot-relative token), and
   treat a PID whose start time does not match as stale.

Tests: timeout path raises LockTimeoutError (not OSError) and leaves no dangling
fd (assert via os.fstat raising on the fd or fd-count accounting); concurrent
edit-lock acquisition admits exactly one owner; a stale lock with a recycled-PID
token is reclaimed.

issue.title: Atomic writes and locking for MRU, history, and axe error state
issue.description:
Durable state files written with truncate-then-write and unlocked
read-modify-write cycles, all verified:

1. src/sase/history/vcs_macro_mru.py `_save_vcs_macro_mru` (~line 263): plain
   `open(mru_file, "w")` + json.dump. This file is the source of truth for the
   current project (see src/sase/current_project.py module docstring) and is
   written on every launch (`record_vcs_macro_usage`) and by the prune path in
   `load_launchable_vcs_macro_mru_pairs`, from multiple processes (TUI, headless
   launches, `set_current_project`). A reader racing the truncate gets invalid
   JSON → treated as empty → the next writer permanently wipes the MRU (and with
   it the current-project selection). Fix: write via unique mkstemp +
   `os.replace` (follow the pattern in src/sase/history/prompt_store.py), and
   serialize the read-modify-write in `record_vcs_macro_usage` and the prune path
   with an flock sidecar lock.
2. Same truncate-write pattern in src/sase/history/hook.py `_save_hooks` (~line
   70) and src/sase/history/command.py (~line 78): convert both to temp+replace
   (locking optional but preferred; at minimum eliminate the
   corruption-on-crash/race window).
3. src/sase/axe/state.py `atomic_write_json` (~lines 45-66) uses one
   deterministic temp name (`path.with_suffix(".tmp")`), so concurrent writers
   (orchestrator + each lumberjack process call `append_error` in
   src/sase/axe/_state_scheduler.py ~line 175 on the shared recent_errors.json)
   interleave writes in the same temp file and can install garbage JSON; the
   loser's rename failure is swallowed. Fix: use `tempfile.mkstemp(dir=...,
   prefix=...)` like src/sase/notification_gates/durability.py already does, and
   protect `append_error`'s read-modify-write with an flock so concurrent errors
   are not lost.

Keep behavior on read unchanged (corrupt/missing files still degrade to
None/empty). Tests: concurrent-writer test (threads or processes) showing no
corrupt JSON and no lost entries for the MRU and recent_errors paths; a
crash-window test (kill between open and write is hard — instead assert the
implementation never truncates the target in place, e.g. by checking the target's
content is always one of the two valid states while a writer loops).

issue.title: Chat-catalog cache lock handling and bead migration idempotency
issue.description:
Two verified sqlite defects:

1. src/sase/history/chat_catalog_provenance/cache.py `open_catalog_cache`
   (~lines 30-48): the rebuild path catches `sqlite3.DatabaseError` —
   but `sqlite3.OperationalError` ("database is locked") is a subclass, and
   `_connect` uses a short busy timeout, so plain cross-process contention is
   misdiagnosed as corruption and `_discard_broken_cache` unlinks a database
   another process has open mid-transaction (its commit lands on the orphaned
   inode and is lost; both processes then pay a full head rescan). Fix: treat
   lock contention as transient — re-raise or retry `sqlite3.OperationalError`
   lock errors (match the "database is locked" family, or check
   `sqlite3.DatabaseError and not OperationalError` plus the
   malformed/not-a-database messages) and only discard on genuine corruption;
   consider raising the busy timeout. Add a regression test: hold a write
   transaction from one connection, open the cache from another, and assert the
   db file is NOT unlinked and the second open either waits or fails without
   destroying state.

2. src/sase/bead/_db_migrations.py `_migrate_issue_types` (~lines 224-270): in
   sqlite3 legacy autocommit mode the `CREATE TABLE _issues_new` DDL commits
   immediately while the following INSERT...SELECT opens the implicit
   transaction. If the INSERT fails (legacy row violating the new CHECKs) or the
   process dies before `conn.commit()`, `_issues_new` persists while the guard
   (`"'plan'" in create_table_sql` of `issues`) still reports "not migrated" —
   so every subsequent `init_db` raises "table _issues_new already exists" and
   the bead mirror is wedged until manual repair. Fix: `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS
   _issues_new` before the CREATE so the rebuild is restartable; audit the other
   table-rebuild migrations in the same file for the same pattern and apply the
   same guard where missing. Also make `init_db` (src/sase/bead/db.py ~lines
   28-40) close its connection when `run_migrations` raises (try/finally or
   closing contextmanager). Tests: simulate the half-migrated state (create
   `_issues_new`, keep old-schema `issues`) and assert init_db now completes the
   migration; assert no connection leak on a failing migration (e.g. monkeypatch
   a migration to raise and assert the connection is closed).

LANDING AUDIT + FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE (sase-1sb.land): NOT READY TO CLOSE. Two epic-caused defects remain; a tale will fix them and close the epic.

Verified: all 7 phases plus nested child epic sase-1sb.2.1 (4 phases) are closed; every child note was read. All three DECISIONS are honored: provenance (SASE_PROMPT_AUTHORSHIP gate in preprocess_prompt_late, macros still expand); digest_trust (sase-1sb.2.1, sunset flag local_config_command_trust, retire task sase-1sc); autoquote (shlex-quoting Jinja env with a | raw opt-out, WORD [A-Za-z0-9._-]+, AGENT allows a leading @). Source checks: linked/sidecar clone dirs use require_safe_path_component and the five log helpers use sase_project_dir; CheckoutMarker validates its fields; git revisions are validated and push uses --end-of-options; AGENT_ENV_VARS includes SASE_AGENT_NAME; MRU/hook/command/axe JSON writes are atomic, with flock on the MRU and append_error; the chat-catalog cache re-raises OperationalError and uses a 5s busy timeout; _migrate_issue_types drops _issues_new first; init_db closes its connection on failure. The test_db_migrations split (51466616d2) kept the restart regression in test_db_migrations_rebuild.py. epic-symbols: none.

REMAINING EPIC WORK:
(1) sase-1sb.5 edit-lock ownership race (DISCOVERED ISSUE note #1) is still on master 2b53bb0c7f. A deterministic probe that delays the first writer's os.write until a second acquire returns gives ['first:owner', 'second:owner']: an O_EXCL file is visible empty, _read_edit_lock returns None, and the contender reclaims it as stale. release_edit_lock also unlinks unconditionally, so a reclaimed owner can delete its successor's lock.
(2) sase-1sb.1 regression: render_prompt_template replaces only the first occurrence of each placeholder (str.find), so a prompt template that interpolates {{ step._raw }} twice leaves a literal __SASE_MODEL_OUTPUT_<nonce>_0__ token in the prompt. Verified by probe.

INTEGRATION: reviewed every non-epic commit since 6cdb74c3e6, including d0dc942c16's siblings, 1087ccd7f1 continuation provenance, the auto-restart launcher resubmit (7665654aaa/d237c84204), a49dac15ca monitor follow-up, and the processor/config/loader/migration-test splits. 1087ccd7f1 tracks authored-request capture text, not command-substitution authorship, so there is no conflict. The healer relaunch passes origin=generated, so with_launch_provenance stamps authorship=agent (fail-closed; accepted). No new multi-writer state or project-dir joins bypass the epic's helpers. No core drift affects the epic.

FOLLOW-UPS:
- sase-1sb.5 note #1 (TUI x-row lifecycle flake): duplicate of sase-1sg (same test, same line-274 signature, confirmed in ToolRun 9fc932a5 stdout). +1 recorded, no new task.

Probe: field/_data/loop executed, _raw protected. This predates the epic and is outside the audited _raw/_response scope, and fixing it needs a design that keeps prompt_part macro expansion (with_q_and_a/with_feedback) and Jinja conditionals working, so new task sase-1sn (bug, large, ready). The placeholder conditional/filter semantics are recorded there as design context.
